llm.description: The carbohydrate balance adds the share of fixed carbon allocated to storage and subtracts basal and growth-related respiration, carbon reused for lipid synthesis, and carbon redirected to lipids under nitrogen deficiency.
llm.quote: The assimilated carbon that has not been used to produce functional biomass is first stored in carbohydrates as shown in R₃ of eq (2). The degradation of carbohydrates is categorized into three types based on the carbon flow direction: (1) the carbon loss during respiration (R₄, R₅), (2) the carbon reuse for lipid synthesis during nitrogen-available conditions (R₆), and (3) the carbon redirection to lipid synthesis under nitrogen deficiency (R₇). The carbohydrate respiration rate includes two components: a basal-level rate (R₄) and a growth-related rate (R₅). R₄ is based on the first-order relationship with the respiration rate constant m_c adjusted by I_avg_R to account for the photoinhibition of respiration.

llm.quote: Following prior modeling work, we linked the Chl-a synthesis rate to the nitrogen uptake rate via the maximum Chl-a:N ratio θ. To account for the light adaptation effect, θ is regulated by I_avg via an exponential function.
